purpose: Research-only handoff for nums 341, 342, 344-353, and 355-362 in data-disney.js. Built from live Common Sense Media refetches of catalog srcUrl pages. Do not treat as production data until reviewed and transformed through the official workflow.

contentFlagModel.mappingNote: This refetch preserves CSM's current visible category label and proposes the nearest app level. Production catalog edits should be made only by the follow-up importer/reviewer.

entries.title: Swiss Family Robinson

violence.summary: Pirate attacks and survival peril include sword fights, cannon fire, rifles, explosives, booby traps that kill or injure pirates, animal attacks, and two brothers fighting over the same girl.

language.summary: CSM does not surface language content.

romance.summary: Teen brothers joke about wanting to see girls, compete for a teen girl's attention, and there is some kissing.

drinking.summary: Father and sons share wine at a table, and the youngest son takes a sip from his father's glass.

handoffNotes: CSM notes that the violence is bloodless but realistic-looking for an older Disney adventure.

violence.summary: Comic action includes pratfalls, henchmen bonking heads and being knocked out, two head-on car crashes without injuries, and gunshots fired during a chase.

language.summary: CSM does not surface language content.

romance.summary: CSM does not surface sex, romance, or nudity content.

drinking.summary: Wine appears in a beaker during an experiment, and police give a sobriety test after a car crash.

entries.title: The Love Bug

language.summary: CSM does not surface language content.

romance.summary: A man ogles a saleswoman's legs while she holds a suggestive sign.

drinking.summary: Herbie is given Irish coffee and joked about as hungover, adults get drunk on Irish coffee, characters drink sherry, wine, and champagne, cigarettes appear, and there are period jokes about hippies seeming high.

handoffNotes: Suicide-imitation scene involving Herbie should be specifically called out in prose.

entries.title: Bedknobs and Broomsticks

violence.summary: War backstory and Nazi threat frame the danger; CSM also notes cartoon soccer violence, one knife threat, and a potentially scary finale with ghost-like armored knights fighting machine-gun-wielding Nazis.

language.summary: The older boy tells his siblings to shut up.

romance.summary: Miss Price and Professor Browne have mild flirtation and a suggested future marriage; animated fish dance cheek-to-cheek.

drinking.summary: A cartoon fish smokes a cigar, and an adult tells a child he wants to go to the pub for a drink.

handoffNotes: Orphaned-by-war setup and Nazi battle sequence may need age-context prose.

entries.title: Charley and the Angel

violence.summary: Near-fatal accidents, car crashes, gunfire, a child forced to drive a getaway car, a partner knocked out, kids held at home, a shoot-out, a car chase, guns drawn by police, and a machine gun all contribute to the violence signal.

language.summary: CSM labels language as none but lists mild insults such as "loonybird," "lounge lizard," "yacking broad," and "boob."

romance.summary: Romance and adult innuendo include teen dating, hugging and kissing, all-night dancing, a woman sent to keep Charley company, a bedroom undressing interruption, elopement anxiety, newlywed giggling, and a passionate goodbye kiss.

drinking.summary: Bootlegging liquor is a subplot, an alcoholic lemonade mistake occurs, gangsters smoke, Charley smokes a pipe, and several jokes refer to sobriety or drinking on the job.

handoffNotes: This is one of the heavier entries in the slice, with both gun violence and bootlegging context.

language.summary: CSM does not surface language content.

romance.summary: Two characters develop a romance and kiss on-screen.

drinking.summary: One man appears drunk after waking from sleep, slurring and wobbling, and characters occasionally smoke cigarettes.

handoffNotes: Nightmare sequence may play scarier than the otherwise comic tone.
